You're doing an adversarial, skeptical audit of a cold-email system just built this session for Nxeon (a real hosting/VPS/game-server business). Do NOT assume anything works correctly — verify by reading the actual code and, where relevant, querying the actual production Postgres database directly. Report concrete, specific findings (file:line, actual query results), not general impressions.

## Context

`lib/coldemail/*.ts` (18 files: analytics, classify, compliance, dns, engagement, feedback, import-spec, import.ts, inbox-match, inbox-send, lead-store, leaddb, rotation, sender.ts, templates, threading, warmup, webhooks) implements a full cold-email engine: lead import with consent tracking, warmup ramping, send scheduling, DKIM-signed delivery through a dedicated isolated relay (separate domain `trynxeon.com`, separate IP, own DKIM key — NOT the platform's main transactional mail), open/click tracking, and reply/inbox polling. `worker/index.ts` runs 4 sweeps on a schedule inside the always-on `nxeon-worker.service`: `coldEmailSendSweep` (2min), `coldEmailWarmupSweep` (15min), `coldEmailRollupSweep` (10min), `coldEmailInboxPoll` (2min).

There are currently 6 `ColdCampaign` rows (all `DRAFT` status, nothing has sent yet — `cold_email_sending_enabled` setting is off): "Local Businesses — Shared Hosting (Variant A)", "...Variant B", "No Website — Free Site with Hosting", "Agencies — VPS/Dedicated Reseller", "Gaming Cafes & Esports", "MSP/Dev/SaaS — VPS & Dedicated". Each has a 4-step `SequenceStep` sequence (Day 0/3/10/17). One `Brand` row (id `cmsobesr3000hhlbruydiad0y`), one `SendingDomain` row (trynxeon.com), one `Inbox` row (`hello@trynxeon.com`, real encrypted SMTP/IMAP creds pointing at a real dedicated relay VM at 51.79.168.98 and Mailcow at mail.nxeon.cloud respectively).

**Already found and fixed this session** (so you don't need to re-find these, but DO verify the fixes are actually correct/complete):
1. `buildMessage()` in `lib/coldemail/sender.ts` was wrapping cold-email HTML in the transactional `wrapEmail()` shell, which hardcoded a wrong postal address and a false "you have a Nxeon account" claim underneath the correct compliance footer. Fixed with a new `wrapColdEmailHtml()` function (just committed, check `git log -1 -- lib/coldemail/sender.ts` for the exact diff).
2. A stale `ColdCampaign` ("Nxeon Outreach", now deleted) was pointing at the SAME source list that got split into two new campaigns — meaning if it had ever been activated, it would have double-sent to all 4,221 contacts in that list. It's been deleted. Verify no other campaign has this same "overlapping target list" landmine (query: which contacts belong to more than one campaign's target list right now, and is any overlap large/systemic vs. small/incidental).

## What to actually audit — be thorough and adversarial

1. **Read `lib/coldemail/sender.ts` end to end.** Look for: injection risks (is `{{token}}` substitution in subject/body safe against a malicious value in a Contact field, e.g. could a contact's own `fullName` or `business.name` break out of the template or inject extra headers/HTML?), whether `markdownToHtml`'s escaping is actually complete, whether the DKIM/SMTP transport logic correctly falls back or fails loudly if an Inbox has no credentials configured (per the code's own comment: "a blank host is the single guard the poller/sender check" — verify this guard actually exists everywhere it needs to).
2. **Read `lib/coldemail/compliance.ts`, `warmup.ts`, `rotation.ts`.** Verify the daily-cap/warmup-ramp math is actually enforced correctly (can a bug let the send sweep exceed `currentRampCap` or `dailyCap`?), verify the complaint-rate circuit breaker (`sendingPaused`) actually gets checked before every send, not just at campaign start.
3. **Read `worker/index.ts`'s 4 cold-email sweep call sites.** Verify they're actually correctly gated by `cold_email_sending_enabled` (does turning that setting off truly stop everything, including warmup/rollup, or just the send sweep?). Check for any race condition risk if two sweep runs overlap (e.g., the 2-minute send sweep firing again before a prior slow run finishes).
4. **Query the database directly** for data-hygiene issues beyond what's already been found:
   - Any campaign whose target list has 0 contacts, or whose `SequenceStep` rows are missing/incomplete (e.g., a step with empty `bodyMarkdown`)?
   - Any contact with `emailStatus` already `DEAD` or a `Suppression` match sitting inside an active campaign's target list (should have been excluded)?
   - Any obviously-malformed email in the campaign target lists (control characters, no `@`, etc. — one zero-width-space contact was already found: `%e2%80%8bbikes@pedalitforward.org`; check the actual raw contact row and whether there are more like it)?
   - Do the `{{company}}` merge-field lookups actually resolve for every contact in every campaign, or will some contacts get literal `{{company}}` text in their email because `business.name` is null/empty (check `Contact.business` join — is every contact reliably linked to a `Business` row with a non-empty `name`)?
5. **Read `app/admin/coldemail/**` (the just-cleaned-up admin UI, 6 sections) and confirm the "Send test email" / preview functionality (if any exists) actually uses the SAME `buildMessage()` code path as the real send — a common bug class is a preview feature drifting out of sync with the real send path.
6. **Check the `unsubscribe` route** (`app/api/coldemail/unsubscribe/route.ts` if it exists) — does it actually work end-to-end (mark the contact as unsubscribed/suppressed so future sends skip them), and is the HMAC token verification (`unsubscribeToken`/verification) actually secure against tampering (can a token be modified to unsubscribe a DIFFERENT contact than the one it was issued for)?
7. **Check test coverage**: run the existing `test/coldemail-*.test.ts` suite and report the actual pass/fail result — don't just assume it's fine because a prior session mentioned it passed.

## Constraints

- Read-only investigation — do not modify any code or database rows. This is purely a verification/audit pass; report findings for a human to act on.
- If you want to run a read-only SQL query, use `sudo -u postgres psql nxeon -c "..."` directly (matching this session's established pattern) — do NOT write/update/delete anything.
- Report findings as a prioritized list: which are real bugs that would cause actual harm if sending were turned on today, which are minor/cosmetic, and which are just things worth knowing (not bugs, just observations). For each real bug, give the exact file:line and a concrete reproduction/evidence (a query result, a code snippet), not a vague description.

content.text:
## Cold-Email System Audit — Findings

I read every file in `lib/coldemail/*.ts`, `worker/coldemail*.ts`, the admin UI, the unsubscribe route, ran the test suite, and queried prod Postgres directly. Three of the findings below are **launch-blocking** and were not on the "already found" list — they defeat the entire point of building an isolated sending domain.

### CRITICAL — would cause real harm if `cold_email_sending_enabled` is flipped on today

**1. The bulk send sweep uses the platform's transactional SMTP, not the dedicated isolated relay.**
`worker/coldemail.ts:437` calls `getTransport("nxeon-smtp")` → `lib/coldemail/sender.ts:325-341` (`loadSmtpConfig()`), which reads the **same** `Setting` rows (`smtp_host`/`smtp_user`/...) used by `lib/mailer.ts` for password resets and invoices. Verified in prod DB: `smtp_host=10.20.0.10`, `smtp_user=noreply@nxeon.cloud`. Meanwhile the real dedicated relay lives on the `Inbox` row: `smtpHost=51.79.168.98`, `smtpUser=relay@trynxeon.com` — and it IS used correctly, but only by the unrelated 1:1 reply path (`lib/coldemail/inbox-send.ts:91-97`, which builds a fresh `NxeonSmtpTransport` from `inbox.smtpHost/smtpUser/smtpPassEnc`). The bulk sweep builds **one shared transport once per sweep** (line 435-441) and reuses it for every rotation-selected inbox, so every message goes out authenticated as `noreply@nxeon.cloud` over `10.20.0.10` while claiming `From: hello@trynxeon.com`. This will either get rejected by Mailcow (envelope/auth mismatch) or — worse — actually relay, misaligning SPF/DKIM for trynxeon.com (whose SPF is scoped to `51.79.168.98`) and commingling bulk cold-outreach traffic with the platform's real transactional mail stream, which is exactly what `ALWAYS_PROTECTED_DOMAINS` (`lib/coldemail/compliance.ts:339`) exists to prevent — just via a code path that guard never touches.

**2. Every tracking/unsubscribe link in a cold email points at the protected platform domain, not the isolated one.**
`buildMessage()` (`lib/coldemail/sender.ts:239`) defaults `base = opts.base ?? appUrl()`, and `appUrl()` (`lib/email-render.ts:69-71`) returns `process.env.APP_URL ?? "https://nxeon.cloud"`. Prod `.env`: `APP_URL=https://nxeon.cloud`. The only real call site, `worker/coldemail.ts:321-328`, never passes `base`. I reproduced this live: a rendered message came out with
`List-Unsubscribe: <https://nxeon.cloud/api/coldemail/unsubscribe?token=...>` and click/open-tracking URLs on `nxeon.cloud` too. So every open pixel, click-redirect, and the one-click unsubscribe link a recipient sees is served from `nxeon.cloud` — the exact domain `evaluateSendEligibility`'s "not a protected/platform domain" check (`lib/coldemail/compliance.ts:397-441`) is supposed to keep clear of cold outreach. That check only validates the From/sending domain — it never validates the link base URL, so this gap is invisible to the eligibility gate. Net effect: any recipient, security gateway, or URL-reputation crawler immediately sees `nxeon.cloud` in the email, unmasking the "separate" brand and putting the main site's domain reputation at exactly the risk the isolated relay was built to avoid.

Both (1) and (2) are wiring bugs in `worker/coldemail.ts`, not in the well-tested pure `lib/coldemail/*.ts` functions — which is why all 118 existing tests pass cleanly (I ran `test/coldemail-{phase3,sender,dns,leaddb,compliance,inbox}.test.ts` directly) without catching either.

### HIGH

**3. Reply-To routes real prospect replies away from the mailbox the reply pipeline actually watches.** Prod `Brand.replyTo = "hello@nxeon.cloud"`, never overridden per-inbox in `loadBrandRotationPool` (`worker/coldemail.ts:90-97`) or `buildMessage` (`sender.ts:277`). But `coldEmailInboxPoll` (`worker/coldemail-inbox.ts`) only polls the `Inbox` row's own IMAP mailbox — `hello@trynxeon.com` via `mail.nxeon.cloud`. A prospect hitting "reply" will send to `hello@nxeon.cloud`, which nothing in the cold-email pipeline reads. Result: the reply-detection → auto-stop-sequence → classify → webhook chain (built specifically for this) will never fire for real replies; contacts who reply keep getting Day-3/10/17 follow-ups, and interested leads can be missed.

**4. The bounce/complaint feedback loop that the auto-pause/circuit-breaker logic depends on is dead in prod.** `app/api/coldemail/feedback/route.ts:22-25` refuses every request when `COLDEMAIL_FEEDBACK_SECRET` is unset — and it is unset in `/opt/nxeon/.env` (confirmed by grep). No Mailcow FBL forwarder or SES SNS subscription targets it. The only `DeliverabilityEvent` types the send path itself writes are `SENT`/`DEFERRED` (from `FAILED`) — see `worker/coldemail.ts:357-363, 376-383`. True `HARD_BOUNCE`/`SOFT_BOUNCE`/`COMPLAINT` events — which `evaluateInboxAutoPause`/`evaluateDomainAutoPause` (`worker/coldemail-deliverability.ts:332,352`) and the complaint circuit breaker (`lib/coldemail/feedback.ts:193-211`) key off of — can currently only arrive via a manual admin action. So the documented safety net (auto-pause on bounce/complaint spikes) is code-complete but has no live data feed today; it will not protect anything until this is wired up.

### MEDIUM

**5. Consent is enforced only in the UI dry-run, never in the real send path.** `previewCampaign` (`lib/actions-coldemail.ts:607-680`) computes and displays a `missingConsent` bucket, but `scheduleCampaignSends`/`processDueSends` (`worker/coldemail.ts:189-390`) never check `ConsentRecord` at all, and neither does `evaluateSendEligibility`. Currently harmless — I confirmed via query that every contact in every active campaign's list has ≥1 `ConsentRecord` — but it's a latent gap: nothing stops a future import (consent recording is opt-in, `recordConsent=false` by default, `lib/coldemail/import.ts:300`) from landing zero-consent contacts in a list that then get emailed with no warning at send time.

**6. Markdown-link injection via contact/business fields.** `substitute()` runs before `markdownToHtml()`, and `markdownToHtml`'s link regex (`sender.ts:91-93`) operates on the already-escaped string, so a `business.name`/`fullName`/`title` value containing literal `[label](https://...)` becomes a real, tracking-wrapped `<a href>` in the rendered email. Reproduced: `business.name = "Acme [click here](https://evil.example/phish)"` rendered as a live clickable link routed through `nxeon.cloud/api/coldemail/track/click/...`. Not exploitable by the recipient, but is exploitable by whatever populates `Business.name`/`Contact.fullName` (scraped/imported lead data) — low-likelihood but worth knowing. Separately verified as **safe**: HTML `<script>` injection is properly neutralized by `esc()` before markdown formatting, and CRLF header-injection attempts (tested with `\r\nBcc:` in both subject and fullName) are neutralized by nodemailer's own RFC 2047 subject encoding — no injected header actually reaches the raw MIME.

### MINOR / data hygiene (in addition to the already-found zero-width-space contact)

- **3 more malformed emails** sitting in active campaign lists, root-caused to the same overly-loose `EMAIL_RE = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/` at `lib/coldemail/import.ts:175,204`: `%20office@kindredpest.com` (Variant A), `%20fahed.ahmed999@gmail.com` (Variant B), `.legacyri@gmail.com` (Variant B) — all clearly scraper/URL-decoding artifacts, will hard-bounce.
- **A/B test isn't actually varied on step 4.** `SequenceStep` bodies for "Local Businesses (Variant A)" and "(Variant B)" are byte-identical (verified by MD5) on step 4 ("last note") — same length, same hash — while steps 1-3 differ. The final follow-up touch isn't being A/B tested.
- **Small, incidental list overlap**: only 2 contacts (out of ~7,100) sit in more than one active campaign's target list (one each between Variant A/"No Website" and Variant B/"No Website") — nothing like the deleted stale-campaign landmine, but worth a manual dedupe before launch.
- All other DB hygiene checks came back clean: no campaign with 0 contacts, no `SequenceStep` with a missing/empty body, no `DEAD`-status or suppressed contact sitting in an active list, and every contact reliably joins to a `Business` row with a non-empty `name` (so `{{company}}` will never render literally).

### OBSERVATIONS (not bugs)

- The public unsubscribe route (`app/api/coldemail/unsubscribe/route.ts`) is correctly implemented and tamper-resistant: HMAC-signed `contactId:brandId` token, constant-time verify, RFC 8058 one-click POST supported, idempotent. One quirk: `claims.brandId` is decoded but never consulted — it always writes a `GLOBAL` suppression regardless of which brand's link was used (safe-by-default, just means the `BRAND`-scope suppression tier is unreachable from this endpoint).
- No feature renders a true end-to-end preview via the real `buildMessage()` path. The two "preview" surfaces are a numeric recipient-count dry-run (`previewCampaign`, no rendering at all) and a template-library sample preview (`renderTemplatePreview`, `lib/coldemail/templates.ts:258-262`) that reimplements token substitution independently rather than reusing `sender.ts`'s `substitute()`. The postal-address-duplication bug fixed this session was caught by manual inspection, not by any repeatable tool — a similar regression could slip through unnoticed again.
- Worker loop (`worker/index.ts:1474`, `for (;;) { await ... }`) is fully sequential — no realistic overlap risk between sweep runs within one process. `cold_email_sending_enabled=false` correctly makes `coldEmailSendSweep` return immediately (`worker/coldemail.ts:407`); warmup/rollup sweeps intentionally keep running while the switch is off since they only maintain state and never send — by design, not an oversight.
- Test suite: all 118 tests across the 6 `coldemail` test files pass. They thoroughly cover the pure `lib/coldemail/*.ts` math/rendering functions but do not (and structurally cannot) catch findings #1-3 above, since those live in `worker/coldemail.ts`'s DB-driven wiring and actual prod `Brand`/`Inbox`/env configuration, not in the pure functions under test.
